Where people are living in space right now

The only two places above you tonight with people inside them.

Open the trip: Where people are living in space right now

Two places, and only two

Right now there are exactly two homes above your head with people inside them. Everything else up here is a machine.

The International Space Station

About the size of a football pitch, and moving at nearly eight kilometres a second. It goes all the way round the Earth every ninety-three minutes, so the crew see fifteen or sixteen sunrises a day.

Tiangong

China's station, about a fifth the mass, and newer. Three people live here at a time, in a low orbit like the other one's, a few hundred kilometres up.

Two specks, one planet

Most of the time they are thousands of kilometres apart. Two specks going round one planet, and that is the whole of humanity that does not live on the ground.

Everything is drawn where it really is, from CelesTrak orbital elements and the planets’ own orbits (astronomy-engine).
